covr performance audit

Source: performance-audit.md

Audit of covr at 7e5599e (3.6.5.9002, main on 2026-11-08), compared with covr 3.5.1, 3.6.0, 3.6.4 and 3.6.5 from CRAN and with the commits on main that changed performance since 3.6.5. Scripts are in performance-audit/ and their summarized output in performance-audit/results/.

Summary

  • On main, coverage costs 1.1–1.6x the uninstrumented install + tests. For Luminescence (16,158 traces, 19.8 million evaluated expressions) package_coverage() takes 175 s against 107 s for R CMD INSTALL plus the tests. Nearly all of the extra time is in the test process: +64 s running the tests and +4 s instrumenting the package when it is loaded. For the small packages the fixed costs dominate and the overhead is 0.7–1 s.
  • report() is the slowest part of covr by far. It takes 354 s for Luminescence, twice as long as computing the coverage, and 6 s for checkmate. 84% of that time goes to htmltools writing out a tag per line of source. A prototype that builds the same table as strings takes 0.31 s. It has been like this in every version measured (314–383 s).
  • traced_files() is quadratic in package size. It splits the whole concatenated package source once for every file. On Luminescence that takes 1.7 s per call, and exclude(), tally_coverage(), percent_coverage(), per_line() and report() each call it at least once. Splitting once takes 0.09 s and gives identical results.
  • Every evaluated expression costs 1.1–1.3 µs in covr:::count(), 25–50x a cheap base R operation. That adds up to 22 s of Luminescence’s tests. A third of it is the isTRUE(.current_test$record) check, and a .Call() counter costs 27–30 ns.
  • Branch coverage (#279) would add about 6.5% to Luminescence’s test time at today’s cost per call. if conditions run 8.6 million times, 43% of all counts, in all three packages (40–43%). With a C counter the cost would be about 0.3 s.
  • History. The R >= 4.4 regression (#567) is confirmed: on R 4.4.3, Luminescence takes 2,517 s with covr 3.6.4, 204 s with 3.6.5 (12x) and 179 s with main (14x). Main is 12–14% faster than 3.6.5 on Luminescence, through #643 (merging 6.8 s → 0.6 s) and #644 (−18 s in the test process). For covr measuring its own coverage, #668 took the run from 61 s to 220 s, more test changes took it to 397 s, and d277880 (#711) brought it back to 80 s. #682 added 21%.

Recommendations, ranked by gain for the effort and risk

# Change Measured or estimated gain Effort / risk
1 Build report()’s source table as strings, not a tag per line Luminescence 354 s → ≈8 s (table 288 s → 0.31 s); checkmate 6 s → <1 s Small / low
2 Split the concatenated source once in traced_files() 1.72 s → 0.09 s per call; −1.6 s in package_coverage() and in each of percent_coverage(), tally_coverage(), zero_coverage(), print(); −4.8 s in report() Small / low
3 Decide whether to record tests when instrumenting, not in every count() count() 1.1–1.3 µs → 0.65–0.77 µs; ≈ −9 s of Luminescence’s tests Small / low
4 Index the parse data once in parse_children() up to −2 s of the 4.1 s instrumentation in each process that loads Luminescence Small–medium / low
5 Count in C: .Call(<symbol>, <index>) 27–30 ns per count instead of ≈1.1 µs: ≈ −22 s (−15%) of Luminescence’s tests; branch coverage almost free Medium–high / medium
6 Document sharding the tests across CI jobs, combining with c() With 4 shards Luminescence takes ≈64 s per job instead of 175 s (estimate) Docs only / none
7 Build to_cobertura()’s XML as strings Part of its 9.3 s on Luminescence (53% is in xml_add_child()) Small / low

Measured and not worth changing: trace file serialization (0.5 s to save, 0.1 s to merge), the installation (no slower than a normal install), and turning off the byte-code JIT (3% faster, within noise).

Setup

  • Machine: WSL2 (Linux 6.18) on an Intel i7-12700KF, 20 logical CPUs, 16 GB shared with other work. All timings are wall clock. Up to four benchmark processes ran at once, so expect about ±5% noise between runs. Medians of 2 runs; the individual runs are in results/summary.md.

  • R 4.3.3 (/usr/bin/R, Ubuntu build), 4.4.3 and 4.6.2 (rig). Each R version has its own library of dependencies (P3M binaries; the same versions of testthat 3.3.2 and htmltools 0.5.9) and a separate library for each covr version, installed from the CRAN archive. Main is installed from git archive HEAD.

  • Benchmark packages, built from CRAN source tarballs:

    Package Code Traces Evaluated expressions in the tests Tests
    forcats 1.0.1 R 736 9,697 149
    checkmate 2.3.4 R + C 879 33,718 169
    Luminescence 0.9.25 R + C++ (Rcpp) 16,158 19,849,339 247

  • Every covr version runs the tests the same way: package_coverage(type = "none", code = "Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = 'true'); testthat::test_dir(<installed tests>, load_package = 'installed', stop_on_failure = FALSE, ...)"). NOT_CRAN matters. Without it, 237 of Luminescence’s 247 tests skip and coverage is 15% instead of 90%. Luminescence has 1 failure and 4 errors with current dependencies, and rjags (a Suggests) can’t be installed, so its tests skip.

  • Skipped:

    • covr 3.5.1, 3.6.0 and 3.6.4 can’t be loaded on R 4.6 (undefined symbol: SET_BODY; fixed in 3.6.5 by #587).
    • Luminescence with covr 3.5.1 and 3.6.0 on R 4.4.3, which would take about 40 minutes per run. R/parse_data.R, the cause of #567, is identical in 3.5.1, 3.6.0 and 3.6.4 (same md5), so 3.6.4 stands in for them. forcats and checkmate were run with all versions.
    • report() is only timed in the first run of each combination. It takes 5–6 minutes for Luminescence.

1. Where performance stands on main

End to end (R 4.6.2)

Package Without coverage: install + tests package_coverage() Ratio report() afterwards
forcats 1.4 + 2.6 = 4.0 s 5.0 s 1.25x 1.2 s
checkmate 2.4 + 6.9 = 9.3 s 10.0 s 1.08x 6.2 s
Luminescence 21.3 + 85.9 = 107.2 s 175.0 s 1.63x 353.8 s

Phases

Each phase of package_coverage() was run separately (bench-phases.R), with a normal install and test run of the same package as the baseline. The test process loads the installed covr main (covr_in_child in results/summary.md).

Phase (seconds) forcats checkmate Luminescence
Baseline R CMD INSTALL 1.4 2.4 21.3
covr install (-O0 --coverage, keep.source, keep.parse.data) 1.3 2.2 19.4
Baseline load namespace 0.03 0.01 0.15
Load + trace_environment() 0.15 0.4 4.1
Baseline tests 2.6 6.9 85.9
Tests, instrumented 3.0 7.2 150.3
save_trace() 0.01 0.03 0.5
merge_coverage() 0.00 0.01 0.1
run_gcov() — 0.1 0.2
as_coverage() + exclude() 0.06 0.2 2.7
package_coverage() end to end 5.0 10.0 175.0
percent_coverage() 0.04 0.2 2.6
tally_coverage() 0.03 0.2 2.6
zero_coverage() 0.03 0.2 2.6
print() 0.2 0.5 3.4
coverage_to_list() 0.04 0.2 2.4

report() 1.2 6.2 353.8
  • Install. The instrumented install is not slower than a normal one: -O0 offsets --coverage and keeping the sources.
  • gcov takes ≤0.2 s for these packages, which have few compilation units. #611 (3.6.5) and #712 (main) targeted packages with many.
  • The test process takes 69 s longer (load +4 s, tests +64 s, saving the trace +0.5 s). The install is 2 s faster and the main process steps add 3 s. The next section breaks down the test process.

Where the test process spends the extra time (Luminescence)

From the Rprof profile (10 ms sampling) of the instrumented test process (results/profile-Luminescence-test-process.txt), 138 s sampled:

Cost Seconds Share Evidence
covr:::count() 22.4 16% 1.13 µs × 19.85 M counts. Includes 5.3 s in isTRUE()
JIT compilation of instrumented functions (cmpfun) 17.7 13% Instrumented functions lose their install-time bytecode. Includes 3.9 s adding constants to the constant pool (putconst)
Instrumentation at load 4.2 3% trace_calls() 3.3 s, of which impute_srcref() → parse_children() 2.0 s; get_parse_data() 0.19 s; replacements_S4() 0.24 s
Rest of the +64 s ≈24 Slower execution of the larger instrumented bodies (if (TRUE) { covr:::count(key); expr } around every expression), not attributable from the profile

With the JIT off (R_ENABLE_JIT=0, results/jit-and-branch-counts.txt) the instrumented tests take 143.0 s against 147.6 s with it on, and the uninstrumented tests take 82.8 s either way. The time spent compiling roughly equals what the compiled code saves, so turning off the JIT gains nothing.

Memory

Process forcats checkmate Luminescence
Test process, baseline (peak RSS) 123 MB 128 MB 755 MB
Test process, instrumented, after save_trace() 128 MB 146 MB 854–875 MB
Main process after package_coverage() 89 MB 116 MB 186 MB (3.6.5: 265 MB)
Main process after report() 139 MB 263 MB 1,008–1,317 MB
Trace files 0.05 MB 0.07 MB 5.35 MB in 4 files (largest 1.36 MB)

Instrumentation adds 4–16% to the test process. report() is again the outlier. It raises the main process from 186 MB to over 1 GB, and it is the peak memory of the whole run.

  • #567 / #588 (fixed in 3.6.5). On R 4.4.3, covr ≤3.6.4 is 12x slower on Luminescence (2,517 s against 204 s with 3.6.5). This is close to the 2,395 s against 170 s reported in #567. The time is all in the test process (run_code 2,487 s), where every nested conditional recomputed the parse data of the whole package. Smaller packages show it too: checkmate takes 12.9–13.5 s with ≤3.6.4 against 9.7 s with 3.6.5 (+33%), and forcats 5.1–5.3 s against 4.6 s. R 4.3.3 is unaffected (197 s with 3.6.4). On R 4.3.3 checkmate is slower with every covr version, because the uninstrumented tests are slower on the Ubuntu build of R.
  • 3.5.1 → 3.6.4 changed nothing measurable apart from that regression.
  • 3.6.5 → main: Luminescence takes 12–14% less time (217 → 186 s on R 4.6.2, 204 → 179 s on R 4.4.3, 187 → 171 s on R 4.3.3), and the main process uses 186 MB instead of 265 MB after package_coverage().
  • report() has taken 5–6 minutes in every version. Dropping DT in #725 didn’t change that, because the per-line tags were already there.

3. Recommendations

1. report(): build the source table as strings

report() creates a <tr> with three <td>s and a <pre> for every line of every file: 66,339 rows for Luminescence. In the profile (results/profile-Luminescence-report.txt, 344 s sampled), 328 s are in htmltools::save_html() → renderTags(), and 288 s (84%) in collapseBuffer() → paste() inside htmltools’ textWriter. Building the tags (report_html()) takes only about 16 s; writing them out is the problem [INFERENCE: the profile doesn’t show why collapseBuffer() is so expensive at this size; it looks like the text buffer is collapsed again and again as the tags are written].

microbench-post.R has a prototype, source_table_html(), that builds the same rows with vectorized paste0() and htmltools::htmlEscape() and wraps the result in HTML():

Step (Luminescence) Time
renderSourceTable() + renderTags() (current) 287.7 s
Prototype + renderTags() 0.31 s
to_report_data() (per_line() + percent_coverage()) 7.1 s

This would take report() from 354 s to about 8 s, and to about 3 s together with recommendation 2. It also removes most of the 1 GB peak. file_report_html() uses the same renderSourceTable(). The risk is in escaping, which htmlEscape() handles the same way as the tags. The existing report tests would catch changes in the markup.

2. traced_files(): split the package source once

Each traced file of an installed package has a srcfilealias whose lines are the whole concatenated package source, with #line directives. traced_files() calls getSrcLines() and a rex regex with two captures on all of those lines for each file. That is O(files × package lines): 144 traced files × 67,555 lines for Luminescence. traced_files() is called by exclude() (inside package_coverage()), tally_coverage() (through non_code_lines()), per_line(), percent_coverage(), zero_coverage(), print(), to_cobertura(), coverage_to_list() and report(). In the profiles of percent_coverage() and tally_coverage(), it accounts for 72–74% of their time.

The split_once() prototype in microbench-post.R splits the source with the existing split_on_line_directives() once per original srcfile, keyed by its address, and stopifnot() checks that the result is identical:

Luminescence Time
traced_files() (current) 1.723 s
Split once 0.094 s

With this change package_coverage() would take 1.6 s less, and each post-processing call would take 1.6 s less per traced_files() call it makes: about 2.6 s → 1 s for percent_coverage(), and 4.8 s less in report(). The regexes in non_code_lines() are not the problem: replacing rex::re_matches() with grepl() saves only 0.011 s (0.036 → 0.025 s).

3. count(): decide whether to record tests when instrumenting

count <- function(key) {
  .counters[[key]]$value <- .counters[[key]]$value + 1L
  if (isTRUE(.current_test$record)) count_test(key)
}

From microbench.R (byte-compiled loops of 10^6 iterations, median of 5, minus an empty loop):

Per call R 4.3.3 R 4.4.3 R 4.6.2
x + 1 22 ns 42 ns 46 ns
covr:::count(key) 1,115 ns 1,238 ns 1,315 ns
isTRUE(.current_test$record) alone 329 ns 313 ns 333 ns
count() without the isTRUE() check 648 ns 705 ns 769 ns
.Call(<native symbol>, <index constant>) C counter 30 ns 27 ns 29 ns
Instrumented 3-statement function, overhead per count 1,114 ns 1,106 ns 1,471 ns
  • The ::: lookup costs 58 ns and is not the problem.
  • The nested replacement .counters[[key]]$value <- ... costs 444 ns.
  • isTRUE() is a closure call on every count, and the profile confirms it: 5.3 of count()’s 22.4 s in the Luminescence test process.

covr.record_tests is set by the load hooks before trace_environment() runs, so trace_calls() could emit covr:::count_and_record(key) when tests are recorded and a count() without the check otherwise. That makes count() 40% cheaper, about −9 s of Luminescence’s tests, for a small and local change.

4. Instrumentation at load: index the parse data

Every process that loads the instrumented package pays for its instrumentation again. For Luminescence that is 4.1 s against 0.15 s for a normal load, and its run loaded the package in 4 processes (4 trace files). Tests, examples and vignettes also run in separate processes, as do tests that start callr or forked workers. In the profile, 2.0 of the 4.2 s are in impute_srcref() → parse_children(). For each conditional, that compares line1, line2, col1, col2 and token against every row of the file’s parse data, and then subsets it with pd$parent == expr_id. The parse data itself is cheap since #644: get_parse_data() takes 0.19 s, and diagnose-parse-fallback.R found no fallback to the slow whole-package getParseData() path on R 4.6.

Keying the per-file parse data once by paste(line1, col1, line2, col2) for expr tokens, and splitting the children by parent, would make each lookup O(1) and save up to 2 s per process for Luminescence (estimate from the profile). A bigger step would be instrumenting once, at install time, and loading the instrumented functions in each process. That is a large change to how covr hooks into packages, and it is not proposed here.

5. Count in C

A .Call() to a native routine, with the routine’s address and the counter’s integer index as constants in the call, costs 27–30 ns, 40x less than count(). The prototype in microbench.R checks that the C counter reaches the expected count. For Luminescence this would save about 21 of the 22.4 s in count(), and the smaller constants could also reduce the 3.9 s of putconst during JIT compilation [INFERENCE: not measured].

The cost is a redesign of the counters:

  • counts kept in a growable C array, indexed from the trace key;
  • save_trace() and merge_coverage() reading the counts from it;
  • recording tests (count_test()) kept on a separate R path;
  • forked processes are fine, since they copy the array.

Do it after recommendation 3, and before or together with branch coverage, which multiplies the number of calls (next section).

Expected cost of branch coverage (#279)

The planned opt-in branch coverage adds one call for each evaluated if. phase-child.R counts how often each if condition ran in the tests, using the counter of the condition in the instrumented function bodies (results/jit-and-branch-counts.txt):

Package if statements if evaluations All counts Extra calls
forcats 154 4,094 9,697 +42%
checkmate 208 13,468 33,718 +40%
Luminescence 3,510 8,620,002 19,849,462 +43%

The expected cost for Luminescence’s 150 s of instrumented tests:

Cost per branch call Extra time Increase
Today’s count(), 1.13 µs +9.7 s +6.5%
Today’s overall overhead per count (64 s / 19.85 M = 3.2 µs) +28 s +19%
count() without the isTRUE() check (rec. 3), 0.7 µs +6 s +4%
C counter (rec. 5), 30 ns +0.3 s +0.2%

Each branch call should not repeat the isTRUE(.current_test$record) check (rec. 3). The forcats and checkmate overhead stays under 0.1 s in every case.

6. Sharding tests in CI

For Luminescence, the costs paid once per job are about 19 s to install, 4 s to instrument each process and about 3 s to post-process. The 150 s of tests divide among the shards. With 4 shards a job would take ≈ 19 + 4 + 150/4 + 3 ≈ 64 s instead of 175 s [INFERENCE: estimated from the phases, not run]. covr can already combine the results of the shards with c() (c.coverage() on main). Each shard can run package_coverage(type = "none", code = testthat::test_dir(..., filter = <shard>)) and save the result. A vignette section or an example workflow would cover it without changes to covr. Running the tests in parallel workers within one job (testthat’s Config/testthat/parallel) should also work, since each worker saves its own trace, but each pays the 4 s load cost [INFERENCE: not tested].

7. to_cobertura()

It takes 9.3 s for Luminescence. xml2::xml_add_child() accounts for 4.6 s, 3.2 s of it setting attributes, because nodes are added one at a time; tally_coverage() takes 2.3 s (results/profile-Luminescence-to_cobertura.txt). Writing the XML as strings, as in recommendation 1, would remove most of the xml2 time. This is low priority: it is 5% of a Luminescence run, and much less in smaller packages.

Not worth changing

  • Trace files: save_trace() takes 0.5 s and merge_coverage() 0.1 s for Luminescence. In microbench.R, portable_srcfiles() takes 0.21 s and saveRDS() with gzip 0.30 s (1.6 MB). Without compression it takes 0.07 s but the file is 9.8 MB. The counts alone would serialize to 1.1 MB; the rest is srcrefs and source lines.
  • Byte-code JIT: see above. Turning it off saves 3%, within noise.
  • Install: covr’s install takes as long as a normal install (19.4 s against 21.3 s for Luminescence).

Commands

The scripts take the benchmark directory (/tmp/covr-bench here) as an argument and leave everything in it. Before heavy runs, mem-ok 4000 was checked, and each run was capped with memcap 6G.

# Libraries: dependencies (P3M binaries) and one library per covr version
# (3.5.1, 3.6.0, 3.6.4, 3.6.5 from the CRAN archive, main from HEAD) for each R
sh performance-audit/setup.sh /tmp/covr-bench
# covr at the commits of the development history (R 4.6.2)
sh performance-audit/setup-commits.sh /tmp/covr-bench 4.6.2 \
  v3.6.5 853f3df^ 853f3df 9183955 c0df663^ c0df663 39b6848^ 39b6848 \
  7d763f3^ 7d763f3 d277880^ d277880 9328a71 02798cb^ 02798cb HEAD

B=/tmp/covr-bench
PKGS="$B/src/forcats_1.0.1.tar.gz $B/src/checkmate_2.3.4.tar.gz $B/src/Luminescence_0.9.25.tar.gz"

# Released versions x packages x R versions, 2 runs each
VERSIONS="3.5.1 3.6.0 3.6.4 3.6.5 main" TIMEOUT=5000 \
  sh performance-audit/run-versions.sh $B 4.3.3 2 $PKGS
VERSIONS="3.5.1 3.6.0 3.6.4 3.6.5 main" TIMEOUT=5000 \
  SKIP="4.4.3-3.5.1-Luminescence 4.4.3-3.6.0-Luminescence" \
  sh performance-audit/run-versions.sh $B 4.4.3 2 $PKGS
VERSIONS="3.6.5 main" TIMEOUT=5000 sh performance-audit/run-versions.sh $B 4.6.2 2 $PKGS

# Development history: Luminescence at each commit and its parent
OUT_SUBDIR=history REPORT=false TIMEOUT=3000 \
  VERSIONS="e734fdf 853f3df 9183955 f1208d1 c0df663 7d9b5ea 39b6848 0159c7e 7d763f3 1b44f08 d277880 9328a71 9ba4bc2 02798cb" \
  sh performance-audit/run-versions.sh $B 4.6.2 2 $B/src/Luminescence_0.9.25.tar.gz

# covr measuring its own coverage at the commits around #668, #682 and #711
sh performance-audit/bench-self.sh $B 4.6.2 2 v3.6.5 c0df663^ c0df663 39b6848^ 39b6848 d277880^ d277880 HEAD

# Phases on main, with a profile of one more instrumented test run;
# the JIT and branch counts
L=$B/lib/4.6.2
for p in $PKGS; do
  R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
    performance-audit/bench-phases.R $B $p 2 $B/out/phases
  R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
    performance-audit/bench-child-variants.R $p 2 $B/out/variants/$(basename $p .tar.gz).rds
done

# Microbenchmarks and profiles (Luminescence coverage and trace from the phases)
R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
  performance-audit/microbench.R $B/out/phases/Luminescence-trace.rds   # also on 4.3.3, 4.4.3
R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
  performance-audit/microbench-post.R $B/out/phases/Luminescence-coverage.rds
R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
  performance-audit/microbench-parse.R $B/out/phases/Luminescence-coverage.rds
R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
  performance-audit/profile-post.R $B/out/phases/Luminescence-coverage.rds $B/out/profiles/Luminescence
R_LIBS=$L/covr-main:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file \
  performance-audit/diagnose-parse-fallback.R $B/src/Luminescence_0.9.25.tar.gz
for sha in d277880 9328a71; do for p in $PKGS; do
  R_LIBS=$L/covr-$sha:$L/deps /opt/R/4.6.2/bin/Rscript --no-init-file performance-audit/trace-size.R $p
done; done

# Tables
Rscript --vanilla performance-audit/summarise.R $B > performance-audit/results/summary.md
Rscript --vanilla performance-audit/summarise-profile.R $B/out/phases/Luminescence-child.Rprof 30
Script What it does
setup.R, setup.sh Dependency and per-version covr libraries for each R version
setup-commits.sh covr at given commits
run-versions.sh, bench-versions.R Time package_coverage() with main-process steps measured by trace() (Rprof only samples CPU time, so it misses waiting for the install and test processes), then the post-processing functions
bench-phases.R, phase-child.R Each phase of package_coverage() on main and the uninstrumented baseline, peak RSS, counts, if evaluations, and a profile of the test process
bench-child-variants.R Tests with the JIT on and off, instrumented and not
bench-self.sh covr’s own coverage through shim_package.sh
microbench.R count() and alternatives, trace serialization
microbench-post.R traced_files(), non_code_lines() and report() with prototypes
microbench-parse.R Parse data with and without token text
profile-post.R, summarise-profile.R Profiles of the post-processing functions
diagnose-parse-fallback.R Counts fallbacks to the slow getParseData() path
trace-size.R Size of the trace files
summarise.R The tables in results/summary.md
